items.title: Protocol Completes: Wholesome Endeavours, Places to Avoid, and Real Fear of Even Small Faults

items.zh: 謂於種種善品加行，若於正法受持讀誦；若於尊長修和敬業，參覲承事；若於病者起慈悲心，殷重供侍；若於如法宣白加行，住慈悲心，展轉與欲；若於正法請問聽受，翹勤無墮；於諸有智同梵行者，盡其身力而修敬事；於他善品常勤讚勵；常樂為他宣說正法；入於靜室，結跏趺坐，繫念思惟。如是等類，諸餘無量所修善法，皆說名為善品加行。彼於如是隨所宣說善品加行，如其所應，於所應作、於如所作，即於此中如是而作。由是作故，不為世間之所譏毀，不為賢良、正至、善士、諸同法者、諸持律者、諸學律者之所呵責。如是名為於諸善品加行處所成就軌則，隨順世間，不越世間；隨順毘奈耶，不越毘奈耶。若於如是所說行相軌則差別悉皆具足，應知說名軌則圓滿。云何名為所行圓滿？謂諸苾芻，略有五種非所行處。何等為五？一、唱令家，二、婬女家，三、酤酒家，四、國王家，五、旃荼羅、羯恥那家。若於如是如來所制非所行處，能善遠離；於餘無罪所有行處，知時而行。如是名為所行圓滿。云何名為於微小罪見大怖畏？謂於諸小、隨小學處，若有所犯，可令還淨，名微小罪。
items.en: Regarding various wholesome endeavours: upholding, reciting the true Dharma; attending on and serving elders through the practice of communal harmony; showing compassion and earnest care towards the sick; properly announcing matters in formal assembly, resting in compassion, and conveying consent when unable to attend; questioning and receiving the true Dharma with diligence, never idle; serving fellow practitioners of wisdom with the full strength of one's body; constantly praising and encouraging others' wholesome endeavours; delighting in teaching the true Dharma to others; and entering a quiet chamber, sitting cross-legged, and fixing the mind in contemplation. …What is called perfected conduct? It is that monks, in brief, have five kinds of place unsuited to their conduct … the household of one who proclaims [the slaughter of livestock]; the household of a prostitute; the household of a wine-seller; the household of a king; the household of an outcaste or a dog-killer [or jailer]. …What is called seeing great danger in even the slightest fault? It is that, regarding minor and subsidiary-minor points of training, should any transgression occur, it can be restored to purity — this is called a slight fault.

items.zh: 於諸學處現行毀犯，說名為罪；既毀犯已，少用功力而得還淨，說名微小。由是因緣，名微小罪。云何於中見大怖畏？

items.title: Three Fears That Guard Against Complacency, and a Lifetime of Continued Study

items.zh: 謂作是觀：勿我於此毀犯因緣，無復堪能得所未得、觸所未觸、證所未證。勿我由此近諸惡趣，往諸惡趣。或當自責，或為大師、諸天、有智同梵行者以法呵責。勿我由此遍諸方維惡名、惡稱、惡聲、惡頌遐邇流布。彼於如是現法、當來毀犯因生諸非愛果，見大怖畏。由是因緣，於小、隨小所有學處，命難因緣亦不故犯。或時、或處失念而犯，尋便速疾如法發露，令得還淨。如是名為於微小罪見大怖畏。云何名為受學學處？謂於先受別解脫戒，白四羯磨受具戒時，從戒師所，得聞少分學處體性；復從親教、軌範師處，得聞所餘別解脫經；總略宣說過於二百五十學處，皆自誓言：一切當學。復從所餘恒言議者、同言議者、常交往者、有親愛者聞所學處，復於半月常所宣說別解脫經聞所學處，一切自誓：皆當修學。以於一切所應學處皆受學故，說名獲得別解律儀。從此以後，於諸學處，若已善巧，便能無犯。設有所犯，尋如法悔。
items.en: One reflects thus: may I not, through the cause of this transgression, lose the capacity ever to attain what has not yet been attained, to touch what has not yet been touched, to realise what has not yet been realised. …May I not, through this, draw near to or go towards the unfortunate rebirths; may I not bring reproach upon myself, or be reproached in accordance with the Dharma by the Teacher, by the gods, or by wise fellow practitioners. …May I not, through this, have an evil name, an evil report, an evil reputation, or evil verses about me spread far and near in every direction. …What is called training in every point of training? It is that, having first received the prātimokṣa precepts … one vows: "I shall train in all of them." …Because one trains in every point one should train in, this is called attaining the prātimokṣa restraint. From this point onward, having become skilled in these points of training, one is thereby able to be free of transgression; should any transgression occur, one promptly confesses it in accordance with the Dharma.

items.zh: 若諸學處未得善巧、未能曉悟，由先自誓願受持故，得於今時求受善巧，欲求曉悟。於如前說諸所學處，從親教師或軌範師，如先請問。既得善巧及曉悟已，隨所教誨無增無減，復能受學。又於尊重及等尊重所說學處，若文、若義能無倒受。如是名為受學學處。如是廣辨戒律儀已。云何應知此中略義？

blocks.text: The rest of the sixfold discipline: the settings for wholesome practice, places a monastic should avoid, and the attitude towards small faults.

Protocol extends to the "settings for wholesome practice": upholding and reciting the Dharma, respecting elders, caring for the sick, giving consent for formal acts, asking for teaching. Venerable Miào Jìng: when someone is ill, they entrust you to convey their consent to the assembly's formal act.

Five places: the houses of proclaimers, of prostitutes, of wine-sellers, of kings, and of outcastes. Venerable Miào Jìng: the "proclaimer" kills sheep and goes about announcing mutton for sale, since there were no newspapers. (Days 133 and 135 met the same list.)
One sees "great danger in the slightest faults". Venerable Miào Jìng: these are minor offences (duṣkṛta); in a broad reading, everything except the four root precepts.

The renunciant thinks: may I not, through this fault, lose the chance "to attain the unattained, touch the untouched, realise the unrealised"; may I not draw near bad rebirths; may I not suffer an evil report. Venerable Miào Jìng: attaining the unattained is stream-entry; touching the untouched, the second and third fruits; realising the unrealised, arhatship.

"Undertaking the training" means continuing to study the precepts throughout one's life. Master Cháng Bǎi: the Buddha said ordinary people forget what they learned within fourteen days, so the precepts are recited every half month. Venerable Miào Jìng: studying the precepts after ordination is also "receiving" them.

quiz.q: What wholesome endeavours does the treatise list?
options: upholding the Dharma, respecting elders, caring for the sick, formal announcements and consent, inquiry, serving the wise, encouraging others, teaching, and sitting in meditation
quiz.why: The treatise lists upholding and reciting the Dharma, respecting elders, caring for the sick, formal announcement and consent, asking and receiving the Dharma, serving wise fellow practitioners, encouraging others' good, teaching the Dharma, and sitting cross-legged in contemplation. Master Cháng Bǎi: anything done within the Three Jewels can be a wholesome endeavour.

quiz.q: The English renders "展轉與欲" as "conveying consent when unable to attend." Who is absent, per the masters?
options: Miào Jìng: someone else is ill and entrusts you to convey their consent; Cháng Bǎi: you yourself cannot attend and send consent through others (requesting leave)
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: when the assembly performs a formal act, someone ill or otherwise detained entrusts you to convey their consent. Master Cháng Bǎi: when you yourself cannot attend, you must formally announce it and convey consent, in person or through another — requesting leave. The two readings run opposite ways.

quiz.q: What readings do the masters give for "the household of a proclaimer"?
options: Miào Jìng: those who kill sheep and go about announcing it; Cháng Bǎi adds another reading: households of singers, whose amusements disturb concentration
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the proclaimer's household kills sheep and goes everywhere selling mutton — with no newspapers, they had to announce it. Master Cháng Bǎi: another reading is a household of singers, pursuing amusement that disturbs concentration, so one should not go.

quiz.q: What is the range of "slight faults" and how are they purified, per the masters?
options: Miào Jìng: duṣkṛta offenses — though Dunlun's commentary counts all but the four root offenses; Cháng Bǎi: confess to one monk or nun of the same ordination
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: these are duṣkṛta offenses; but Dunlun's commentary takes a broad view — everything except the four root precepts is a minor offence. Master Cháng Bǎi: for such a light offence one need only find a monk or nun of the same precepts, confess, and repent.

quiz.q: Seeing great danger in slight faults, what three reflections does the treatise describe?
options: lest this transgression prevent attaining the unattained; lest it lead to bad rebirths and reproach; lest an evil name and evil verses spread far and near
quiz.why: May I not, through this transgression, lose the capacity to attain the unattained, touch the untouched, realise the unrealized; may I not draw near bad rebirths or be reproached; may I not have an evil name and evil verses spread far and near. Master Cháng Bǎi: small faults accumulating day by day grow immeasurable, and one cannot attain the fruits.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng map "attain the unattained, touch the untouched, realise the unrealized" onto the fruits?
options: attaining is stream-entry; touching is once-return and non-return; realising is arhatship
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "attaining the unattained" — what I never had I now have — is stream-entry. "Touching the untouched" is the second and third fruits. "Realising the unrealized" is the fourth fruit.

quiz.q: Why, per Master Cháng Bǎi, are the precepts recited every half month?
options: the Buddha said people forget what they learned in fourteen days
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the Buddha said ordinary people forget what they have learned in fourteen days, so the precepts are recited every fourteen days — every half month.
